# Markdown Briefing: OCERS 2023 RFP PAS Oversight Scope

## Overview
OCERS requires a **full-time, on-site consultant** to act as an **implementation partner** for the selection and implementation of a new **Pension Administration System (PAS)**. The role combines **project oversight, project management support, staff support, and quality assurance** across the full project lifecycle.

## Core Required Services

### 1. Project Oversight and Management
- Provide overall **project management and quality oversight**.
- Support OCERS through **active participation, review, facilitation, and guidance**.
- Help ensure the PAS is delivered **on time, within budget, and according to requirements**.
- Coordinate with the **Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO)**.

### 2. Planning and Project Definition
- Lead planning related to **requirements definition, solution design, and IT strategic roadmap alignment**.
- Perform **needs and requirements assessments**.
- Facilitate input from departments on PAS needs.
- Incorporate strategic capabilities such as **RPA, ML, AI, and intelligent automation**.
- Develop:
  - **staffing plan**,
  - **IT Strategic Roadmap**,
  - **PAS implementation project plan**,
  - overall **implementation approach**,
  - **milestones and resource requirements**.

### 3. Procurement and RFP Support
- Draft the **RFP(s)** for software and related services.
- Prepare the PAS procurement documentation.
- Coordinate procurement with OCERS staff.
- Support vendor selection, including:
  - **software demonstrations**,
  - **vendor interviews**,
  - **BAFO evaluation**,
  - **final vendor selection**.

### 4. Vendor and Contract Oversight
- Coordinate and manage vendor performance.
- Ensure vendors meet the **requirements matrix** and all RFP obligations.
- Review PAS vendor contracts.
- Work collaboratively with **Procurement, Legal, IT, and Member Services**.

### 5. Implementation Oversight
- Oversee **design, development, testing, training, and deployment**.
- Support conversion strategy for:
  - **data cleansing**,
  - **data migration**,
  - **data conversion**.
- Establish procedures for requirements gathering with OCERS and the PAS vendor.

### 6. Deliverables and Documentation Review
- Provide **project reports and metrics** for status and due-date tracking.
- Review and comment on key deliverables, including:
  - **Statements of Work**,
  - **data conversion and reconciliation plans**,
  - **test plans, scripts, and cases**,
  - **user acceptance plans and criteria**,
  - **project schedules**,
  - **cutover plans and timelines**.

### 7. Governance and Methodology
- Establish and enforce **sign-off procedures** across the system development lifecycle.
- Ensure a rigorous **methodology, plan, and schedule** are defined and followed.
- Ensure schedule changes are properly reflected in project plans.

### 8. Communications, Risk, Issues, and Change Control
- Ensure clear communication of **project status and issues**.
- Manage and escalate issues promptly.
- Identify and address **project risks**.
- Ensure **change control procedures** are followed.

### 9. Quality Assurance and Testing
- Provide ongoing **quality assurance**.
- Develop testing procedures to support a **high-quality implementation**.

### 10. Stakeholder Coordination and Reporting
- Prepare a **monthly oversight status report**.
- Present updates to the **Steering Committee** and **Board of Retirement**.
- Provide updates to external stakeholders when requested.
- Facilitate meetings with employers and third-party vendors.
- Help establish a **common project glossary**.

### 11. Organizational Change and Training
- Provide leadership in **Organizational Change Management (OCM)**.
- Support **staff training** throughout the PAS project.

### 12. Post-Implementation Support
- Provide **post-go-live support**, with scope and duration to be agreed later.

### 13. Additional Project Management Support
- Address other project management issues that may hinder project success.

## Engagement Context
- **Engagement model:** Full-time
- **Work location:** On-site
- **Expected start:** Approximately **February 2024**
- **Estimated duration:** About **3 years**

## Bottom Line
OCERS is seeking a consultant to provide **end-to-end oversight and project management support** for PAS selection and implementation, spanning **planning, procurement, vendor management, implementation governance, QA, reporting, risk/change control, stakeholder coordination, training, and post-implementation support**.

In its September 2023 RFP for Pension Administration Project Oversight and Consultation Services, OCERS requires the consultant to serve as an implementation partner providing full-time, on-site oversight project management, staff support, and quality assurance for the selection and implementation of a new Pension Administration System (PAS).

Key required project oversight services include:

1. Overall project oversight and management
- Provide project management and quality oversight for the selection and implementation of the new PAS.
- Help OCERS manage and oversee the full implementation process through active participation, review, facilitation, and guidance.
- Ensure the new system meets project requirements, stays on schedule, and remains within budget.
- Coordinate with OCERS’ Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO).

2. Planning and early project definition
- Coordinate planning tasks tied to requirements definition, solutions design, and the IT strategic roadmap.
- Perform a needs and requirements assessment.
- Facilitate gathering departmental wants and needs for the new PAS.
- Incorporate OCERS strategic initiatives, including future-oriented capabilities such as Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Machine Learning (ML), Artificial Intelligence, and Intelligent Automation.
- Create a staffing plan.
- Create an IT Strategic Roadmap plan.
- Develop the PAS implementation project plan and overall implementation approach.
- Identify project milestones and resource needs throughout the project.

3. RFP development and procurement support
- Write the RFP(s) for required software applications and/or services.
- Prepare a concise and comprehensive RFP for the new PAS.
- Coordinate the procurement process with OCERS staff.
- Facilitate and advise on vendor selection activities, including:
  - software demonstrations,
  - vendor interviews,
  - evaluation of BAFO submissions,
  - final vendor selection.

4. Vendor and contract oversight
- Coordinate and manage vendors.
- Ensure vendors meet the requirements matrix.
- Ensure PAS vendor(s) satisfy all RFP requirements and have an approach/strategy for each required item.
- Review PAS vendor contracts.
- Perform services cooperatively with OCERS staff, including Procurement, Legal, IT, and Member Services.

5. Implementation oversight
- Oversee and coordinate design, development, testing, training, and implementation activities for the new PAS.
- Work with OCERS and PAS vendor(s) on the overall conversion strategy, including:
  - data cleansing,
  - data migration,
  - data conversion.
- Establish procedures for requirements gathering with OCERS and the PAS vendor.

6. Deliverables management and documentation review
- Provide project management reports and metrics for accurate status and due-date reporting.
- Develop, review, and comment on project deliverables and documentation, including:
  - Statements of Work and task descriptions,
  - data conversion plans and reconciliation procedures,
  - system test plans, scripts, and test cases,
  - user acceptance plans and acceptance criteria,
  - project schedules,
  - cutover plans, timelines, and processes.

7. Governance, approvals, and methodology
- Establish a sign-off process and ensure adequate sign-off procedures are followed throughout the system development life cycle.
- Ensure a rigorous project methodology, plan, and schedule are proposed and followed.
- Ensure any schedule changes are properly reflected in the project plan.

8. Communications, issues, risk, and change control
- Ensure project issues and status are properly communicated.
- Manage project issues and escalate them appropriately and promptly when needed.
- Identify and address project risks for proper management.
- Ensure change control procedures are followed.

9. Quality assurance and testing
- Provide quality assurance as part of the oversight role.
- Develop testing procedures to ensure a high level of quality.

10. Stakeholder coordination and reporting
- Prepare a monthly oversight status report.
- Present the monthly status report to both the Steering Committee and the OCERS Board of Retirement.
- Provide project updates to external stakeholders as requested by the Steering Committee.
- Facilitate meetings and implementation oversight activities with external stakeholders such as employers and third-party vendors.
- Agree on a common glossary of terms for use across project teams.

11. Organizational change and training
- Work with OCERS to provide leadership in Organizational Change Management (OCM).
- Support staff training on the PAS throughout the project.

12. Post-implementation support
- Provide post-implementation support, with the final scope and duration to be mutually agreed upon.

13. Other project management support
- Address other project management issues that could hinder successful completion of the project.

Additional context from the RFP
- The engagement is envisioned as full-time.
- The expected project start date is approximately February 2024.
- The PAS implementation is estimated to take about 3 years.
- The consultant’s services must be provided on-site.

Section 1: Introduction
The Orange County Employees Retirement System (“OCERS”) is requesting proposals from qualified 
firms interested in providing consulting services to aid in the design, selection of, and smooth 
implementation of their new Pension Administration Solution (PAS). This solution will replace their 
current system, V3. The selected consultant will be responsible for providing Oversight Project 
Management services, which will include staff support and quality assurance. These services are vital to 
support the successful implementation of the new PAS. It's worth noting that the selection of the new 
PAS will be made independently of, but simultaneously with, the selection of the implementation 
consultant.
The project's expected start date is approximately February 2024, and the entire PAS implementation 
process is estimated to take around 3 years to complete. OCERS envisions this as a full-time consulting 
engagement.
The primary role of the selected consultant will be to assist OCERS in efficiently managing and 
overseeing the implementation process. This involves active participation, careful review, facilitation, 
and guidance throughout the project. The consultant's goal is to ensure that the new system fulfills all 
project requirements, is completed within the designated timeframe, and remains within the allocated 
budget. The solution may include multiple software solutions that will need to interact with each other. 
Our intention is to have a future proof solution with the ability to grow and incorporate current and 
emerging technologies such as Intelligent Automation.
Questions about this RFP must be submitted in writing by 5:00 p.m., PT, Friday, September 29 to Jim 
Doezie, Contracts, Risk & Performance Administrator, by email at jdoezie@ocers.org or direct to 
Planetbids through this link: https://pbsystem.planetbids.com/portal/56826/bo/bo-detail/109932
Those who wish to be considered must submit their completed proposal by 5:00 p.m., PT, Friday, 
October 20, 2023. Specific instructions for proposal submissions are contained in Section 7 of this RFP. 
Section 2: Background
OCERS was established in 1945 under the County Employees Retirement Law of 1937, providing
members with retirement, disability, death, and cost-of-living benefits. There are approximately 50,000 
members served by OCERS, of which over 19,000 are retirees. OCERS is governed by a nine-member 
Board of Retirement (“Board”), which has plenary authority and fiduciary responsibility for the 
investment of moneys and administration of the retirement system. OCERS has over one hundred 
employees, and the Board appoints a Chief Executive Officer responsible for the agency’s management. 
For additional information about OCERS, please refer to the OCERS website at ocers.org.
Section 3: Scope of Services
The detailed scope of services for this engagement is outlined in the attached Exhibit “B” (“Scope of 
Services”). The primary objectives are to provide OCERS with guidance and project management
oversight in selecting and implementing a new PAS.
The firm selected for this engagement will be expected to meet requirements that include, but are not 
limited to, the following:

1. The firm must have all necessary permits and licenses to perform the requested services and 
must be bonded where applicable. 
2. Minimum insurance coverage must include the following items, and proof of such insurance 
must be provided to OCERS prior to the commencement of work, on an annual basis, and upon

• Commercial General Liability: $2M per occurrence, $2M aggregate
• Automobile Liability: $1M per occurrence, $2M aggregate
• Workers Compensation: $1M per occurrence, $1M aggregate
• Umbrella Liability: $5M per occurrence, $5M aggregate 
• Professional Liability: $2M per occurrence, $3M aggregate
OCERS must be listed as an additional insured on the above policies.
3. The firm shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and 
other items and services necessary to perform all services, tasks, and functions as requested in 
this RFP. 
4. The initial term of the contract awarded pursuant to this RFP will be for a three-year period,
with OCERS retaining the option to renew the contract, on an annual basis, for up to an 
additional three years. The total term of the contract will not exceed six years.

including the regulations of the State of California, Division of Industrial Safety and the 
provisions of the California Labor Code.

Section 1: Introduction
The Orange County Employees Retirement System (“OCERS”) is requesting proposals from qualified 
firms interested in providing consulting services to aid in the design, selection of, and smooth 
implementation of their new Pension Administration Solution (PAS). This solution will replace their 
current system, V3. The selected consultant will be responsible for providing Oversight Project 
Management services, which will include staff support and quality assurance. These services are vital to 
support the successful implementation of the new PAS. It's worth noting that the selection of the new 
PAS will be made independently of, but simultaneously with, the selection of the implementation 
consultant.
The project's expected start date is approximately February 2024, and the entire PAS implementation 
process is estimated to take around 3 years to complete. OCERS envisions this as a full-time consulting 
engagement.
The primary role of the selected consultant will be to assist OCERS in efficiently managing and 
overseeing the implementation process. This involves active participation, careful review, facilitation, 
and guidance throughout the project. The consultant's goal is to ensure that the new system fulfills all 
project requirements, is completed within the designated timeframe, and remains within the allocated 
budget. The solution may include multiple software solutions that will need to interact with each other. 
Our intention is to have a future proof solution with the ability to grow and incorporate current and 
emerging technologies such as Intelligent Automation.

Scope of Services
Pension Administration Project Oversight
OCERS is seeking an implementation partner for this mission critical pension 
administration project. The service required consists of developing and reviewing key 
project management deliverables to ensure that the following are being properly 
addressed:
1. Planning – Coordinating tasks associated with requirements definition, IT strategic 
roadmap, and solutions design.
2. Writing the RFP(s) for the required software applications and/or services. 
3. Coordinate for the procurement process for review and selection of winning
solution with OCERS staff. Additional in-depth details are listed under the 
“Selection and Implementation of New PAS” section.
4. Oversight of New PAS: Coordinate the design, development, testing, and training 
and implementation activities. Ensure that the software vendor(s) satisfies all 
items as listed in the RFP and has an approach/strategy in place to address each 
item as stated. Coordinate with OCERS’ Enterprise Project Management Office 
(EPMO).
5. Establish Sign-Off Process – Ensure that adequate sign-off procedures are 
followed throughout the system development life cycle.
6. Project Deliverables – Provide project management reports and metrics for 
accurate status and due-date reporting to key participants. Develop, review and 
comment on all project deliverables, documentation, etc., e.g.:
• Perform a needs and requirements assessment
• Create a staffing plan
• Create an IT Strategic Roadmap plan
• Manage the project budget
• Coordinate and manage vendors
• Ensure vendors meet the requirements matrix
• Coordination of the following:
• Statement of Work and Task Descriptions
• Data conversion plans and reconciliation procedures
• System test plans, scripts, cases, etc.
• User acceptance plan, acceptance criteria, etc.
• Project Schedule including cutover plans: timelines 
and process
7. Project Methodology, Planning and Scheduling – Ensure that a rigorous methodology,

properly escalated and addressed in a timely manner.

monies and administration of the retirement system. The OCERS Investment Committee is comprised of all the 
members of the Board. OCERS has over ninety employees and the Board appoints a Chief Executive Officer 
who is responsible for the management of the agency. 
The OCERS’ investment portfolio, approximately $21.5 billion in assets as of June 30, 2021, is diversified 
globally and across multiple asset classes. Currently OCERS’ contributions from members and employers are 
largely sufficient to fund the retiree payrolls. OCERS invests in separate accounts, commingled vehicles, funds 
of one, funds of funds, limited partnerships, and co-investments through external investment managers. The 
Investment Committee has delegated to the Chief Investment Officer (CIO) the responsibility to manage the 
investment portfolio subject to Investment Committee approved policies. Further details on OCERS’

Consultant under general direction from the Investment Committee. In all cases, the Consultant and its 
representatives shall offer advice that is solely in the interest of OCERS and perform its duties in accordance 
with the OCERS’ investment guidelines.

conduct due diligence, collaborate with OCERS’ Investment Team and Investment Committee, and attend 
meetings as needed.

alternative assets portfolio, collaborate with OCERS’ Investment Team and Investment Committee, and attend 
meetings as needed.

against losses. The dominant characteristics of the private credit in credit asset class are interest rate risk

These strategies tend to have an element of equity optionality and the return is often driven by an 
illiquidity premium and complexity premium. The equity-like private credit allocation is expected to be
covered by the Private Equity Consultant.
OCERS has a Unique Strategy category for strategies that are differentiated from those in the portfolio’s other 
main asset classes. Given that these types of ideas can have characteristics of multiple or any asset class and 
market type, public or private, the investments in the Unique Strategy category can fall under the purview of

Asset Class Objective and Goals:
• Global Public Equity
The investment objective of the global equity is to achieve consistent positive real returns and to 
maximize long-term total return with prudent levels of risk through a combination of income and 
capital appreciation. OCERS has adopted a style diversified structure that is designed to have 
aggregate equity portfolio characteristics similar to that of the global equity market as represented by 
the MSCI ACWI IMI Index. While passive management is utilized in the more efficient parts of the 
markets, active management is favored for small cap, emerging market equity, etc.
• Private Equity
The objective of the private equity asset class is to provide diversification for the overall portfolio and 
enhance returns; a diversified global portfolio targeting top-quartile managers within each segment of 
the market. The asset class is composed of fund of funds, direct private equity, and non-performing 
and/or equity-like private credit. The asset class is targeting 63% buyout, 25% venture, 7% special 
situations, and 5% other (non-core interests through legacy FoFs); and 64% North America, 20% 
Europe, 13% Asia, and 3% Global. Additionally, 10% of the annual private equity commitments are set 
aside for co-investment opportunities alongside OCERS’ current existing GP relationships. 
OCERS will continue to seek out direct fund investments in top-quartile managers globally. Private 
equity has a pacing plan to deploy $675 million in 2021 and $700 million in 2022. OCERS will also focus 
on top-quartile managers that will provide co-investment opportunities, allowing OCERS to top up on 
“best ideas” while bringing down the total fee load. Co-investments with existing and approved 
General Partners in sizes of $5 to $10 million are approved under the current guidelines.
• Fixed Income
The objective of the fixed income asset class is to diversify equity risk, preserve capital, generate 
income, and in the case of TIPS, protect against inflation. The asset class is broken down into two main 
categories: investment grade bonds and TIPS. The former is mostly actively managed through core and 
core-plus mandates. TIPS are invested in an index fund. 
• Credit
The objective of this asset class is to allow the plan to capture the credit risk premium. Credit has a 7% 
overall target in the portfolio and includes four main sub-asset classes: corporate credit, opportunistic 
credit, emerging markets debt, and performing bond-like private credit. The asset class is targeting 
35% corporate credit and opportunistic credit, 29% emerging markets debt, and 36% private credit.
The corporate credit allocation is made up of corporate bonds and banks loans that are mainly below 
investment grade. Opportunistic credit seeks to deliver returns by taking advantage of periods of 
credit dislocation in public markets. OCERS’ emerging markets debt exposure is predominantly 
expressed through blended mandates in local and external emerging markets sovereign debt. Finally, 
the majority of the private credit exposure is in middle market direct lending and asset based lending.
As for the private credit sub-asset class, it has a pacing plan to deploy $125 to $200 million per year 
across 2 to 3 investments.
• Real Assets: 
The objective of the real assets asset class is to provide diversification for the overall portfolio while 
providing income and an inflation hedge. Real assets has a 5% overall target in the portfolio and 
includes infrastructure, energy, timber, agriculture, and other hard asset strategies. 
Real assets has a pacing plan to deploy $100 to $150 million per year across 2 to 3 investments.

• Real Estate
Within real estate, OCERS targets 60% to core strategies and 40% to non-core strategies with up to 
10% of the real estate allocation permitted to be invested in non-U.S. assets. OCERS will continue to 
move towards a balance of core and non-core real estate investment allocations.
• Risk Mitigation
The objective of the risk mitigation asset class includes protecting against an equity market decline, 
diversifying the total portfolio away from growth risk, and having a positive return over a cycle. The 
asset class is composed of 25% target allocation each to long-term treasuries, global macro, 
systematic trend following, and alternative risk premia. 
• Unique Strategies
The objective of the unique strategies asset class is to enhance return and diversify the risks of the 
OCERS’ portfolio while exhibiting a low correlation to public equity and fixed income markets. This 
portion of the portfolio is reserved for strategies that are truly unique and while differentiated from 
those in the portfolio’s other main asset classes, can have characteristics of multiple or overlapping 
asset classes but are not easily categorized by just one in particular. For this reason, Unique Strategies 
may fall under the purview of any OCERS’ Investment Consultant.
Since there is no target for Unique Strategies, the category will continue to be utilized in an 
opportunistic manner and will continue to evolve over time, likely increasing the OCERS’ portfolio 
exposure to new and niche platforms and strategies in the future.

Asset Class Objective and Goals:
• Global Public Equity
The investment objective of the global equity is to achieve consistent positive real returns and to 
maximize long-term total return with prudent levels of risk through a combination of income and 
capital appreciation. OCERS has adopted a style diversified structure that is designed to have 
aggregate equity portfolio characteristics similar to that of the global equity market as represented by 
the MSCI ACWI IMI Index. While passive management is utilized in the more efficient parts of the 
markets, active management is favored for small cap, emerging market equity, etc.
• Private Equity
The objective of the private equity asset class is to provide diversification for the overall portfolio and 
enhance returns; a diversified global portfolio targeting top-quartile managers within each segment of 
the market. The asset class is composed of fund of funds, direct private equity, and non-performing 
and/or equity-like private credit. The asset class is targeting 63% buyout, 25% venture, 7% special 
situations, and 5% other (non-core interests through legacy FoFs); and 64% North America, 20% 
Europe, 13% Asia, and 3% Global. Additionally, 10% of the annual private equity commitments are set 
aside for co-investment opportunities alongside OCERS’ current existing GP relationships. 
OCERS will continue to seek out direct fund investments in top-quartile managers globally. Private 
equity has a pacing plan to deploy $675 million in 2021 and $700 million in 2022. OCERS will also focus 
on top-quartile managers that will provide co-investment opportunities, allowing OCERS to top up on 
“best ideas” while bringing down the total fee load. Co-investments with existing and approved 
General Partners in sizes of $5 to $10 million are approved under the current guidelines.
• Fixed Income
The objective of the fixed income asset class is to diversify equity risk, preserve capital, generate 
income, and in the case of TIPS, protect against inflation. The asset class is broken down into two main 
categories: investment grade bonds and TIPS. The former is mostly actively managed through core and 
core-plus mandates. TIPS are invested in an index fund. 
• Credit
The objective of this asset class is to allow the plan to capture the credit risk premium. Credit has a 7% 
overall target in the portfolio and includes four main sub-asset classes: corporate credit, opportunistic 
credit, emerging markets debt, and performing bond-like private credit. The asset class is targeting 
35% corporate credit and opportunistic credit, 29% emerging markets debt, and 36% private credit.
The corporate credit allocation is made up of corporate bonds and banks loans that are mainly below 
investment grade. Opportunistic credit seeks to deliver returns by taking advantage of periods of 
credit dislocation in public markets. OCERS’ emerging markets debt exposure is predominantly 
expressed through blended mandates in local and external emerging markets sovereign debt. Finally, 
the majority of the private credit exposure is in middle market direct lending and asset based lending.
As for the private credit sub-asset class, it has a pacing plan to deploy $125 to $200 million per year 
across 2 to 3 investments.
• Real Assets: 
The objective of the real assets asset class is to provide diversification for the overall portfolio while 
providing income and an inflation hedge. Real assets has a 5% overall target in the portfolio and 
includes infrastructure, energy, timber, agriculture, and other hard asset strategies. 
Real assets has a pacing plan to deploy $100 to $150 million per year across 2 to 3 investments.

• Real Estate
Within real estate, OCERS targets 60% to core strategies and 40% to non-core strategies with up to 
10% of the real estate allocation permitted to be invested in non-U.S. assets. OCERS will continue to 
move towards a balance of core and non-core real estate investment allocations.
• Risk Mitigation
The objective of the risk mitigation asset class includes protecting against an equity market decline, 
diversifying the total portfolio away from growth risk, and having a positive return over a cycle. The 
asset class is composed of 25% target allocation each to long-term treasuries, global macro, 
systematic trend following, and alternative risk premia. 
• Unique Strategies
The objective of the unique strategies asset class is to enhance return and diversify the risks of the 
OCERS’ portfolio while exhibiting a low correlation to public equity and fixed income markets. This 
portion of the portfolio is reserved for strategies that are truly unique and while differentiated from 
those in the portfolio’s other main asset classes, can have characteristics of multiple or overlapping 
asset classes but are not easily categorized by just one in particular. For this reason, Unique Strategies 
may fall under the purview of any OCERS’ Investment Consultant.

opportunistic manner and will continue to evolve over time, likely increasing the OCERS’ portfolio

# Markdown Briefing: OCERS 2023 RFP PAS Oversight Scope

## Overview
OCERS requires a **full-time, on-site consultant** to act as an **implementation partner** for the selection and implementation of a new **Pension Administration System (PAS)**. The role combines **project oversight, project management support, staff support, and quality assurance** across the full project lifecycle.

## Core Required Services

### 1. Project Oversight and Management
- Provide overall **project management and quality oversight**.
- Support OCERS through **active participation, review, facilitation, and guidance**.
- Help ensure the PAS is delivered **on time, within budget, and according to requirements**.
- Coordinate with the **Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO)**.

### 2. Planning and Project Definition
- Lead planning related to **requirements definition, solution design, and IT strategic roadmap alignment**.
- Perform **needs and requirements assessments**.
- Facilitate input from departments on PAS needs.
- Incorporate strategic capabilities such as **RPA, ML, AI, and intelligent automation**.
- Develop:
  - **staffing plan**,
  - **IT Strategic Roadmap**,
  - **PAS implementation project plan**,
  - overall **implementation approach**,
  - **milestones and resource requirements**.

### 3. Procurement and RFP Support
- Draft the **RFP(s)** for software and related services.
- Prepare the PAS procurement documentation.
- Coordinate procurement with OCERS staff.
- Support vendor selection, including:
  - **software demonstrations**,
  - **vendor interviews**,
  - **BAFO evaluation**,
  - **final vendor selection**.

### 4. Vendor and Contract Oversight
- Coordinate and manage vendor performance.
- Ensure vendors meet the **requirements matrix** and all RFP obligations.
- Review PAS vendor contracts.
- Work collaboratively with **Procurement, Legal, IT, and Member Services**.

### 5. Implementation Oversight
- Oversee **design, development, testing, training, and deployment**.
- Support conversion strategy for:
  - **data cleansing**,
  - **data migration**,
  - **data conversion**.
- Establish procedures for requirements gathering with OCERS and the PAS vendor.

### 6. Deliverables and Documentation Review
- Provide **project reports and metrics** for status and due-date tracking.
- Review and comment on key deliverables, including:
  - **Statements of Work**,
  - **data conversion and reconciliation plans**,
  - **test plans, scripts, and cases**,
  - **user acceptance plans and criteria**,
  - **project schedules**,
  - **cutover plans and timelines**.

### 7. Governance and Methodology
- Establish and enforce **sign-off procedures** across the system development lifecycle.
- Ensure a rigorous **methodology, plan, and schedule** are defined and followed.
- Ensure schedule changes are properly reflected in project plans.

### 8. Communications, Risk, Issues, and Change Control
- Ensure clear communication of **project status and issues**.
- Manage and escalate issues promptly.
- Identify and address **project risks**.
- Ensure **change control procedures** are followed.

### 9. Quality Assurance and Testing
- Provide ongoing **quality assurance**.
- Develop testing procedures to support a **high-quality implementation**.

### 10. Stakeholder Coordination and Reporting
- Prepare a **monthly oversight status report**.
- Present updates to the **Steering Committee** and **Board of Retirement**.
- Provide updates to external stakeholders when requested.
- Facilitate meetings with employers and third-party vendors.
- Help establish a **common project glossary**.

### 11. Organizational Change and Training
- Provide leadership in **Organizational Change Management (OCM)**.
- Support **staff training** throughout the PAS project.

### 12. Post-Implementation Support
- Provide **post-go-live support**, with scope and duration to be agreed later.

### 13. Additional Project Management Support
- Address other project management issues that may hinder project success.

## Engagement Context
- **Engagement model:** Full-time
- **Work location:** On-site
- **Expected start:** Approximately **February 2024**
- **Estimated duration:** About **3 years**

## Bottom Line
OCERS is seeking a consultant to provide **end-to-end oversight and project management support** for PAS selection and implementation, spanning **planning, procurement, vendor management, implementation governance, QA, reporting, risk/change control, stakeholder coordination, training, and post-implementation support**.
